content.value_statement: React and Next applications need correct renderer setup and safe streaming behavior. This skill guides CSS imports, client boundaries, rendering modes, and migration decisions.
actual_capabilities: Checks whether the host application uses React, Next, or another React-based framework.
Guides installation of markstream-react and only requested optional peer dependencies.
Explains where to import the markstream-react stylesheet.
Selects content or nodes based on streaming, parsing, and AST ownership needs.
Configures streaming and completed-history renderer behavior.
Recommends client-only boundaries for browser-dependent Next integrations.
limitations: Does not install packages or modify project files by itself.
Does not provide full application-specific component implementations.
Does not validate undocumented Markstream APIs or package compatibility.
Trusted HTML and relaxed Mermaid settings require application-level security review.

use_cases.title: Add a React markdown renderer
use_cases.description: Set up markstream-react, import its stylesheet, and choose an initial content-based renderer configuration.

use_cases.title: Build a streaming chat interface
use_cases.description: Configure smooth streaming while tokens arrive and switch to completed-history behavior when a message is final.

use_cases.title: Plan a react-markdown migration
use_cases.description: Assess renderer wiring, scoped overrides, and when to use the related migration guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Start a React integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add markstream-react to this React application. Identify the correct CSS import location and a minimal content-based setup.

prompt_templates.title: Configure a Next client boundary
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Next application structure and recommend the smallest client-only boundary for markstream-react and its browser-only peers.

prompt_templates.title: Tune chat streaming
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure markstream-react for a chat message that streams tokens and then becomes final. Explain the smoothStreaming, fade, and typewriter choices.

prompt_templates.title: Assess a renderer migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this react-markdown usage for migration to markstream-react. Identify required renderer changes, scoped overrides, SSR concerns, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: I need Markstream in a standard React application.
output: Import the stylesheet from the application shell.

output_examples.input: My Next chat message streams, then becomes final.
output: Use automatic smooth streaming while the message streams.
Disable fade during streaming to avoid flicker.
When final, disable smooth streaming and enable fade for completed history.
Keep browser-only dependencies behind a client boundary.

best_practices: Start with content rendering unless another layer already owns parsing or AST transforms.
Use the smallest client-only boundary needed for browser-dependent integrations.
Keep safe HTML policy and Mermaid strict mode unless trusted content has been reviewed.
anti_patterns: Do not enable trusted HTML rendering for untrusted user content.
Do not use smooth streaming for first-screen SSR content unless a blank initial state is intentional.
Do not move to nodes rendering before confirming a need for external AST control.

faq.question: Which applications does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports React 18+, Next, and other React-based host applications.

faq.question: Where should I import the stylesheet?
faq.answer: Import markstream-react/index.css from the application shell or client entry.

faq.question: Should I use content or nodes?
faq.answer: Use content first. Use nodes when another layer owns parsing, AST transforms, or shared AST storage.

faq.question: How should streaming messages behave?
faq.answer: Use automatic smooth streaming while content arrives. Switch to completed-history settings after the message is final.

faq.question: How does this work with Next SSR?
faq.answer: Put browser-only dependencies behind the smallest practical client-only boundary or a non-SSR dynamic import.

faq.question: When can I use trusted HTML or relaxed Mermaid mode?
faq.answer: Use them only for reviewed trusted surfaces and document why the safer defaults do not apply.
